14	"""Triton implementation of ``aten.upsample_bilinear2d`` (NCHW bilinear).
15	
16	Round 2 architecture
17	--------------------
18	Round 1 measured 37.8 ns per output element, exactly linear in the element
19	count and identical for fp16/bf16/fp32.  A target probe showed a contiguous
20	block copy of the same volume needs ~0.03 ms net, so the cost is per-lane
21	addressing: ``tl.load(ptr + <vector of unrelated indices>)`` lowers to
22	per-lane non-affine loads, roughly 300x slower than block transfers.
23	
24	Two kernels are therefore used.
25	
26	``_bilinear_int_kernel`` (fast path)
27	    Taken when ``align_corners`` is False, no explicit ``scales_*`` is given,
28	    the last input stride is 1 and ``OW == 2*IW``.  One program owns ``BR``
29	    whole output rows.  Every memory access keeps a *contiguous minor
30	    dimension*: the two source rows are found from a data-dependent row base
31	    and read along the row (row-gather with a contiguous minor dimension,
32	    which the backend handles well), and the horizontal resample is expressed
33	    as an affine expansion -- output column ``2*k + j`` is selected between
34	    the two interpolants of input column ``k`` on a constexpr axis ``j``, so
35	    no index vector ever addresses memory.  The store is contiguous over the
36	    whole ``(BR, IW, 2)`` tile, i.e. over ``BR`` complete output rows.
37	
38	``_bilinear_flat_kernel`` (general path)
39	    A flat 1-D tile over ``N*C*OH*OW`` with the four neighbours read through
40	    the real input strides; it covers every shape the fast path declines
41	    (non-2x ratios, ``align_corners=True``, 1x1 outputs, non-unit minor
42	    stride, explicit scales).
43	
44	Both kernels reproduce PyTorch's coordinate mapping exactly:
45	``src = idx*(in-1)/(out-1)`` for ``align_corners`` (0 when ``out == 1``),
46	otherwise ``src = max((idx + 0.5)*scale - 0.5, 0)`` with ``scale = 1/scales_*``
47	when given and positive, else ``in/out``; the right/bottom neighbour is
48	``min(i0 + 1, size - 1)``, matching PyTorch's ``i1p`` edge rule.
49	"""
50	
51	import torch
52	import triton
53	import triton.language as tl
54	
55	# tuning knobs (overridable by diagnostics)
56	_TARGET_PROGRAMS = 256
57	_UB_ELEMS = 2048
58	_FLAT_ELEMS = 2048
59	
60	
61	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
62	# fast path: exact 2x horizontal expansion, contiguous minor dimension
63	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
64	@triton.jit
65	def _bilinear_int_kernel(
66	    ptr_o,
67	    ptr_i,
68	    n_rows,
69	    s_n,
70	    s_c,
71	    s_h,
72	    rh,
73	    C: tl.constexpr,
74	    IH: tl.constexpr,
75	    IW: tl.constexpr,
76	    OH: tl.constexpr,
77	    OW: tl.constexpr,
78	    BR: tl.constexpr,
79	    IWP: tl.constexpr,
80	):
81	    pid = tl.program_id(0)
82	    rows = pid * BR + tl.arange(0, BR)
83	    oh = rows % OH
84	    nc = rows // OH
85	    n = nc // C
86	    c = nc - n * C
87	
88	    real_h = tl.maximum((oh.to(tl.float32) + 0.5) * rh - 0.5, 0.0)
89	    h0f = real_h.to(tl.int32)
90	    hl = real_h - h0f.to(tl.float32)
91	    h0 = tl.minimum(h0f, IH - 1)
92	    h1 = tl.minimum(h0 + 1, IH - 1)
93	
94	    base = n * s_n + c * s_c
95	    rr0 = (base + h0 * s_h)[:, None]
96	    rr1 = (base + h1 * s_h)[:, None]
97	
98	    k = tl.arange(0, IWP)
99	    ka = k[None, :]
100	    lm = tl.broadcast_to((ka < IW) & (rows[:, None] < n_rows), (BR, IWP))
101	    il = tl.broadcast_to(tl.maximum(k - 1, 0)[None, :], (BR, IWP))
102	    ir = tl.broadcast_to(tl.minimum(k + 1, IW - 1)[None, :], (BR, IWP))
103	
104	    hl2 = hl[:, None]
105	    h0l2 = 1.0 - hl2
106	
107	    # Two *aligned* row loads only.  A load whose base is off by one element
108	    # costs ~25x more than an aligned one on this backend (measured: 6 loads
109	    # with +-1 taps 21.3 ms vs 2 aligned loads 0.59 ms on the 8.4M-output
110	    # geometry), so the +-1 column neighbours are produced in registers with
111	    # tl.gather, which measured nearly free (0.59 -> 0.69 ms).
112	    v = h0l2 * tl.load(ptr_i + (rr0 + ka), mask=lm, other=0.0).to(tl.float32) \
113	        + hl2 * tl.load(ptr_i + (rr1 + ka), mask=lm, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
114	
115	    vm = tl.gather(v, il, 1)
116	    vp = tl.gather(v, ir, 1)
117	
118	    even = 0.25 * vm + 0.75 * v
119	    odd = 0.75 * v + 0.25 * vp
120	
121	    # (BR, IWP, 2) tile: its row-major order is exactly BR output rows of
122	    # OW = 2*IW contiguous elements.
123	    val = tl.join(even, odd)
124	    j = tl.arange(0, 2)
125	    ooff = (rows * OW)[:, None, None] + (ka * 2)[:, :, None] + j[None, None, :]
126	    om = tl.broadcast_to(
127	        (ka < IW)[:, :, None] & (rows[:, None, None] < n_rows), (BR, IWP, 2)
128	    )
129	    tl.store(ptr_o + ooff, val.to(ptr_o.dtype.element_ty), mask=om)
130	
131	
132	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
133	# general path: flat 1-D tile, neighbours read through the real strides
134	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
135	@triton.jit
136	def _bilinear_flat_kernel(
137	    ptr_o,
138	    ptr_i,
139	    total,
140	    s_n,
141	    s_c,
142	    s_h,
143	    s_w,
144	    rh,
145	    rw,
146	    C: tl.constexpr,
147	    OH: tl.constexpr,
148	    OW: tl.constexpr,
149	    IH: tl.constexpr,
150	    IW: tl.constexpr,
151	    ALIGN_CORNERS: tl.constexpr,
152	    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
153	):
154	    pid = tl.program_id(0)
155	    offs = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
156	    mask = offs < total
157	
158	    ow = offs % OW
159	    row = offs // OW
160	    oh = row % OH
161	    nc = row // OH
162	
163	    if ALIGN_CORNERS:
164	        if OH > 1:
165	            real_h = oh.to(tl.float32) * ((IH - 1.0) / (OH - 1.0))
166	        else:
167	            real_h = tl.zeros([BLOCK], dtype=tl.float32)
168	        if OW > 1:
169	            real_w = ow.to(tl.float32) * ((IW - 1.0) / (OW - 1.0))
170	        else:
171	            real_w = tl.zeros([BLOCK], dtype=tl.float32)
172	    else:
173	        real_h = tl.maximum((oh.to(tl.float32) + 0.5) * rh - 0.5, 0.0)
174	        real_w = tl.maximum((ow.to(tl.float32) + 0.5) * rw - 0.5, 0.0)
175	
176	    h0 = real_h.to(tl.int32)
177	    w0 = real_w.to(tl.int32)
178	    hl = real_h - h0.to(tl.float32)
179	    wl = real_w - w0.to(tl.float32)
180	
181	    h0 = tl.minimum(h0, IH - 1)
182	    w0 = tl.minimum(w0, IW - 1)
183	    h1 = tl.minimum(h0 + 1, IH - 1)
184	    w1 = tl.minimum(w0 + 1, IW - 1)
185	
186	    n = nc // C
187	    c = nc - n * C
188	    base = n * s_n + c * s_c
189	    r0 = base + h0 * s_h
190	    r1 = base + h1 * s_h
191	    c0 = w0 * s_w
192	    c1 = w1 * s_w
193	
194	    v00 = tl.load(ptr_i + (r0 + c0), mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
195	    v01 = tl.load(ptr_i + (r0 + c1), mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
196	    v10 = tl.load(ptr_i + (r1 + c0), mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
197	    v11 = tl.load(ptr_i + (r1 + c1), mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
198	
199	    w0l = 1.0 - wl
200	    h0l = 1.0 - hl
201	    top = w0l * v00 + wl * v01
202	    bot = w0l * v10 + wl * v11
203	    val = h0l * top + hl * bot
204	
205	    tl.store(ptr_o + offs, val.to(ptr_o.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask)
206	
207	
208	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
209	# host side
210	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
211	def _reciprocal_scale(in_size, out_size, align_corners, scale):
212	    """PyTorch ``area_pixel_compute_scale`` (accscalar_t == float32 path)."""
213	    if align_corners:
214	        if out_size > 1:
215	            return (in_size - 1) / (out_size - 1)
216	        return 0.0
217	    if scale is not None and scale > 0:
218	        return 1.0 / float(scale)
219	    return in_size / out_size
220	
221	
222	def _pick_flat_block(total):
223	    if total >= (1 << 20):
224	        return _FLAT_ELEMS
225	    if total >= (1 << 16):
226	        return 1024
227	    if total >= (1 << 12):
228	        return 512
229	    return 256
230	
231	
232	def _pick_rows_per_program(iwp, n_rows):
233	    """Rows per program: bounded by the UB tile budget and by a program count
234	    that keeps per-program launch overhead small."""
235	    cap = max(1, _UB_ELEMS // iwp)
236	    want = max(1, triton.cdiv(n_rows, _TARGET_PROGRAMS))
237	    br = min(cap, want)
238	    br = 1 << (br.bit_length() - 1)
239	    # prefer a divisor of n_rows so the row mask is entirely unnecessary
240	    while br > 1 and n_rows % br != 0:
241	        br >>= 1
242	    return max(1, br)
243	
244	
245	def _resolve(shape, strides, out_size, ac, scales_h, scales_w):
246	    """Resolve everything that depends only on tensor *metadata*.
247	
248	    Only scalars are produced; no tensor, storage or data pointer is cached,
249	    and the caller's cache key contains shape, strides, dtype, output size and
250	    the coordinate options, so a different view or layout derives its own
251	    entry instead of reusing a stale one.
252	    """
253	    N, C, IH, IW = shape
254	    OH, OW = out_size
255	    s_n, s_c, s_h, s_w = strides
256	    n_rows = N * C * OH
257	
258	    rh = _reciprocal_scale(IH, OH, ac, scales_h)
259	    rw = _reciprocal_scale(IW, OW, ac, scales_w)
260	
261	    if (
262	        not ac
263	        and scales_h is None
264	        and scales_w is None
265	        and s_w == 1
266	        and IW > 1
267	        and OW == 2 * IW
268	    ):
269	        iwp = triton.next_power_of_2(IW)
270	        br = _pick_rows_per_program(iwp, n_rows)
271	        return (True, (triton.cdiv(n_rows, br),),
272	                (n_rows, s_n, s_c, s_h, rh, C, IH, IW, OH, OW, br, iwp))
273	    total = N * C * OH * OW
274	    block = _pick_flat_block(total)
275	    return (False, (triton.cdiv(total, block),),
276	            (total, s_n, s_c, s_h, s_w, rh, rw, C, OH, OW, IH, IW, ac, block))
277	
278	
279	_LAUNCH_CACHE = {}
280	
281	
282	def run(input, output_size, align_corners=False, scales_h=None, scales_w=None):
283	    N, C, IH, IW = input.shape
284	    OH = int(output_size[0])
285	    OW = int(output_size[1])

287	    out = torch.empty((N, C, OH, OW), device=input.device, dtype=input.dtype)

302	            out,

305	            s_n,

312	            OH=koh,
